articles.title: Ölhandel: Frankreich wirbt für internationalen Einsatz in Straße von Hormus
articles.teaser: Frankreichs Präsident Macron appelliert an den Iran, eine multinationale Mission zur Sicherung der Schifffahrt zuzulassen. Auch US-Präsident Trump wolle er überzeugen.
articles.image_title: Ölhandel: TOPSHOT - France's President Emmanuel Macron (R) greets Britain's Prime Minister Keir Starmer as he arrives to co-chair a meeting of allies to consider sending a multinational force to ensure security and free-flowing trade in the Strait of Hormuz, at the presidential Elysee Palace in Paris on April 17, 2026. French President Emmanuel Macron and UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer chair a meeting of allies to consider sending a multinational force to ensure security and free-flowing trade in the Strait of Hormuz once the current conflict between Iran and the US and Israel ends. Iran imposed the blockade on the critical shipping bottleneck as soon as the US and Israel launched the war against the Islamic republic on February 28, leading to a surge in global energy prices. Even with a shaky ceasefire in place, the US is now imposing its own blockade on Iranian ports. (Photo by Ludovic MARIN / AFP via Getty Images)

The National Tax and Customs Administration (NAV) conducted criminal proceedings on suspicion of money laundering. On March 5, it took into custody seven Ukrainian citizens, including a former Ukrainian secret service general, as well as two armored cash transport vehicles, according to a statement of the tax authority, cited by national news agency MTI.
